title: Experiment drift logbook: intermittent throughput dip investigation
content:
Purpose:
Quick investigative log for the intermittent throughput dip that started showing up in capacity shadow runs around 2026-09-28. Aim is to capture what we tried this week, early hypotheses, and a concise runbook for replicating the most expressive failures.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Observed a ~18-22% drop in sustained QPS for mixed-sequence workload A on p3d-like nodes when sequence length distribution skews >40% long queries. p95 latency increases non-linearly in the same window.
- Pattern is intermittent: affects about 1 in 6 nodes in a cluster; node-level warmup seems to impact whether it surfaces.
- KV-cache hit rate correlates with impact but is not sufficient to explain magnitude.
- Short-term mitigations: pin batch size to 8 and force prefetch for long sequences during canary. Reduced drop to ~6-8% but increases p50 slightly.

Timeline / notes from runs:
- 2026-09-28 09:00 PT: First shadow run anomalies flagged by synthetic-checker (alert: throughput-delta >15% vs baseline).
- 2026-09-30: Re-ran shadow in staging with identical config -> reproduced on 3/18 nodes (same node ids across runs).
- 2026-10-01: Collected perf counters (SM stall % , L2 miss, PCIe events) via /debug/perf-export for affected nodes; initial glance shows small bump in CUDA kernel launch latency on affected nodes.
- 2026-10-03: A/B experiment: disabled prefix prefetch on affected nodes -> throughput restored to baseline but p95 degraded further. Suggests a prefetch/cache interaction.
- 2026-10-05: Tried pinning worker-thread affinity + forcing constant batcher window (200ms) -> intermittent reproduction rate dropped but still seen on cold-started tasks.

Observations (raw):
- Correlation: KV-cache hit rate drop of 4–6% coincides with throughput loss; but servers with same hit rate sometimes unaffected.
- Affected nodes show 1.2–1.8x higher CUDA kernel queueing time (small absolute ms), and occasional microbursts of CPU syscall latency (syscalls blocking background io thread).
- When prefetch is ON + large batch windows, we see the worst-case. Prefetch OFF reduces bursts but causes more frequent KV misses and raised p50.
- Hot model variant (quantized-int8) shows smaller relative drop than float16 model.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Prefetch + batcher interaction triggers KV-cache eviction thrash under certain request arrival patterns (mixed seq). Eviction causes backend load and kernel queueing.
2) Kernel scheduling variability on older driver nodes (observed in PerfExport) causes occasional stalls that amplify under large batches.
3) Background housekeeping (checkpointing/telemetry flush) stutters coincide with slower serving loop on ~1/6 nodes.
4) Network packet reordering + retransmits for nodes under NLB path -> rare, lower confidence.

Runs / reproduction steps (most reliable):
- Repro script: tools/bench/repro_mixedseq.sh --nodes 6 --seed 42 --long-pct 45 --burst 0.3 --duration 20m
- Baseline config: model=redwood-7b-fp16, batcher.window_ms=120, batcher.max_batch=32, prefetch.kv=true
- Repro that triggers issue: same as baseline but increase long-pct to 45% and set batcher.window_ms=200.
- Observed metric windows: p50 ~18ms -> 21ms (+17%), p95 ~62ms -> 87ms (+40%), sustained QPS down from 240 -> 192 (-20%). KV hit rate drops 3.8%.

Diagnostics captured:
- /debug/perf-export/2026-10-01-node-09.log (attached to ticket ENG-4982)
- strace snippets show background thread fd epoll_wait spikes on affected nodes around reproduction points.
- GPU kernel trace: small kernel-launch latency increases (0.2ms -> 0.6ms) aggregated across tens of launches per request for long sequences.

Immediate mitigations tried (notes):
- Force smaller fixed batch window (120ms): improves throughput but raises p50 for short sequences. Tradeoff acceptable in canary.
- Disable prefix prefetch for test pool: removes large bursts but increases token cost 2–3%.
- Canary routing to int8 variant where possible: less pronounced drop, plan to expand via routing policy if we can't fix infra root cause.

Open actions and owners: (short actionable list)
- Aisha: schedule driver + kernel trace across older firmware machines; include nvidia-smi sampling and nvprof capture for drivers. (due 2026-10-12)
- Daniel: extend PerfExport to include kernel queueing histogram (PR #814) and run 24h background capture on staging. (in progress)
- Maria: run targeted KV-cache stress harness to evaluate eviction thresholds with prefetch on/off. Post findings to ENG-4982. (due 2026-10-11)
- Thomas: test canary routing to int8 variant for select production traffic (safety window + rollback plan). (due 2026-10-09)
- Team: add a small e2e test that simulates mixed-seq arrival patterns to CI smoke so regressions get flagged earlier. (owner: eng-ci)

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Might be worth instrumenting per-request kernel-count, not just aggregated time. If long sequences cause many small kernels, launch overhead dominates.
- Consider a small hybrid prefetch mode: prefetch for top-10 hot prefixes only, leave others lazy. Could reduce eviction noise.
- If driver-level variability is the root cause, rolling upgrades for older nodes should be prioritized before heavy release.

Meeting sync plan (next standup 2026-10-08):
- 5m: quick summary + concrete ask (decide whether to expand int8 canary).
- 10m: Daniel shows PerfExport histograms and PR status.
- 15m: Maria shares KV stress results and top hypothesis.
- 5m: Confirm owners and next steps; schedule deep-dive if needed.

Appendix: quick commands used during debugging:
- Collect perf-export: curl -sS http://node:1234/debug/perf-export > /tmp/nodeX.json
- Kernel trace: sudo nsys profile -o /tmp/trace.nsys-rep --trace=cuda,osrt --duration=60 --capture-range=nvtx
- Repro bench: python tools/bench/mixed_seq_runner.py --config configs/mixed_a.yml --seed 42 --duration 1200

Unresolved questions: (short)
- Why are only some nodes affected even when config is identical? (hardware/driver/firmware?)
- Exact interaction pattern between prefetch and eviction thresholds under mixed arrival; how to simulate cheaply in CI?
- Cost impact of keeping prefetch disabled at scale (token cost vs. availability).

If you want to run the quick repro locally, ping me and I'll drop the docker image + minimal dataset into the team GCR.

-- Aisha
